concern: Forcing a status read after every write may cost an extra hub round trip per switch/select/number change, which is the session churn the H500 hardware brief warns against - the fix is only cheap if the refresh poll would have happened anyway rather than adding one.

The premise assumes the handshake inside 'async with session' is genuinely unbounded; if H500MediaSession or the underlying pytapo socket already sets a connect/read timeout, nothing parks forever and the idea collapses.

The fix only stays cheap if it is a pending-rerun flag; implemented as a plain reload or correlation token it lets two list_recordings calls fly at the hub concurrently, and nothing in tests/test_cards.mjs currently asserts serialization, so the churn could ship unnoticed.

Wrapping the session enter in wait_for cancels a blocked readuntil, but whether pytapo's session closes its writer on cancellation is unverified -- if it does not, every timeout leaks a half-open socket onto the hardware the brief says wedges, which is worse than the parked lock.

The residual claim prices N bogus timestamps as N media sessions, but api.py:614 serialises them behind one lock, so the real cost is a queue of 2-second bounded sessions, not concurrency - unless the preview URL is reachable without a valid signature, an attacker must already be an authenticated HA user, which makes the whole hazard a self-inflicted slow queue rather than a security defect.

The proposed test (a fake client counting iter_recording calls) pins the clamp, but nothing establishes what the correct clamp bound IS - a timestamp range check needs a source of truth for valid clip times, and if that means asking the hub for the recording list first, the fix adds the very session it is trying to prevent.
